name: fpsimd_init
prose: Boot-time initcall (core_initcall(fpsimd_init)) that takes no arguments. Behaviour in order: if cpu_have_named_feature(FP) is true it calls fpsimd_pm_init() then fpsimd_hotplug_init(); these register the CPU PM notifier and the CPU hotplug dead callback only when CONFIG_CPU_PM and CONFIG_HOTPLUG_CPU are respectively enabled, otherwise the corresponding helper is an empty inline. If FP is not present it prints "Floating-point is not implemented" with pr_notice. Then, independently of FP, if ASIMD is not present it prints "Advanced SIMD is not implemented". It then calls sve_sysctl_init() and sme_sysctl_init() and returns 0. The only return statement is the final return 0; there is no error return, and return values of the registration helpers are not examined.
note: Contract cleared: function reads CPU-feature global state and performs registrations and prints, which the old ensures result == 0 contract does not cover (reviewer round 15 right on that). Reviewer round 2 claim (helpers are no-ops without CONFIG_CPU_PM/HOTPLUG_CPU) was already reflected in the prose (fpsimd.c:92-94, 109-111). Slice contains the whole function at 123-141.

name: fpsimd_save_user_state
prose: Static function with no arguments, called with preemption disabled (WARN_ON fires if preemptible() or if FPSIMD is unsupported; execution continues after the warning). It works on this CPU per-CPU fpsimd_last_state (last). Return paths: (1) if TIF_FOREIGN_FPSTATE is set it returns at once and saves nothing; (2) if the SVE save is selected but sve_get_vl() differs from the expected vl, WARN_ON fires, force_signal_inject(SIGKILL, SI_KERNEL, 0, 0) is called on the current task, and it returns without saving SVE or FPSIMD registers and without writing *last->fp_type (FPMR and SVCR/ZA saves already done before this point stay done); (3) otherwise it falls off the end after saving. Before the save step: if FPMR is supported it stores the FPMR register into *last->fpmr; SVE register saving is selected, with vl = last->sve_vl and save_ffr true, when (last->to_save is FP_STATE_CURRENT and TIF_SVE is set) or last->to_save is FP_STATE_SVE; if SME is supported it reads SYS_SVCR and stores the value into *last->svcr (whenever SME is supported, regardless of the ZA bit), calls sme_save_state(last->sme_state, system_supports_sme2()) only when SVCR.ZA is set, and when SVCR.SM is set it forces SVE saving with vl = last->sme_vl and save_ffr = system_supports_fa64(). Final step: if CONFIG_ARM64_SVE is enabled and SVE saving is selected (and the vl check passed) it calls sve_save_state at last->sve_state + sve_ffr_offset(vl) with &last->st->fpsr and save_ffr and sets *last->fp_type = FP_STATE_SVE; otherwise (including SVE saving selected but CONFIG_ARM64_SVE disabled) it calls fpsimd_save_state(last->st) and sets *last->fp_type = FP_STATE_FPSIMD.
note: Reviewer round 15 (SVCR written whenever SME is supported, not only when ZA set) is right: fpsimd.c:216-219. Round 2 (WARN_ON on unbound last) is wrong: there is only a comment at 186, no such WARN_ON; the WARN_ONs at 191-192 test FPSIMD support and preemptible(). Original-rejection claim (SIGKILL return, fp_type not set) is right: 235-243. Slice contains the whole function at 182-253.

name: find_field
prose: Static __init helper. Parameters: cmdline (token text), opt (scratch buffer already holding a prefix of len bytes, normally "<name>."), len, reg and field index f, and v (output). Precondition: reg->fields[f].name is NUL-terminated; opt is writable for indices 0 through len + strlen(name) inclusive; cmdline is readable for len + strlen(name) + 1 bytes (memcmp compares that many bytes). Behaviour: it writes the field name and then "=" into opt after the prefix, then does memcmp of cmdline against opt over len + strlen(name) + 1 bytes. If they differ it returns -1 and *v is not written. If they match it returns parse_hexdigit(cmdline + len + strlen(name) + 1, v): an initial "0x" or "0X" is skipped when present, and the result is 0 with *v set to 0..15 when the next character is a hexadecimal digit and the character after it is NUL or whitespace (later characters are not examined); otherwise -EINVAL and *v is unchanged. Returned values are therefore only -1, -EINVAL or 0. It modifies the opt buffer in all cases.
note: Reviewer round 1 (omits optional 0x) is wrong: the prose already states the 0x skip (idreg-override.c:4-5, parse_hexdigit). Reviewer round 2 (memcmp reads len bytes) is already covered by the readability precondition on cmdline; memcmp at line 25. Prose tightened and return values enumerated.

name: parse_cmdline
prose: Static __init function taking the FDT pointer and the chosen node offset; it returns nothing. It selects at most one top-level string to parse with __parse_cmdline(str, true): get_bootargs_cmdline() yields the bootargs property of the chosen node, or NULL if chosen < 0, the property is missing, or the property is empty. If CONFIG_CMDLINE_FORCE is enabled, or the property is NULL, the built-in CONFIG_CMDLINE string is parsed; if CONFIG_CMDLINE_FORCE is not enabled and the property is non-NULL, the bootargs string is parsed instead (the built-in string is then not parsed). Parsing a string (__parse_cmdline) loops: skip leading whitespace; return if the text starts with "--" followed by a whitespace character; collect a token of non-whitespace characters, with "-" replaced by "_", at most 255 characters per chunk (a longer word is processed as successive 255-character chunks); return when the token is empty (end of string); otherwise call match_options on the token, and then, only when alias parsing is enabled, for each alias whose alias string equals the token (compared with its NUL) parse the alias feature string recursively with alias parsing disabled. match_options tries, for each register in order and each field in order, the prefix "<name>.<field>=" against the token; a field is skipped if the token does not start with that prefix or the rest is not an optional 0x followed by one hex digit that ends the token; for the first field that does match: if the field has a filter that rejects the value its mask bits are set in the override val and cleared in the override mask and the scan continues with later fields; otherwise the mask bits of val are replaced by (value << shift) & mask, the mask bits are set in the override mask, and the scan stops for that token. Here mask covers bits shift to shift + width - 1, with width 4 if the field width is 0.
note: Reviewer round 1 (built-in parsed unless forced) is wrong against the prose, which already says the built-in string is parsed only when forced or when no non-empty bootargs exist (idreg-override.c:135-139). Reviewer round 2 (invalid hex digit still treated as applied) is wrong: find_field returns nonzero for invalid digits and match_options continues (55-56). Whole function and callees are in the slice (31-140).

name: init_sdei_stacks
prose: Static function with no arguments, run at boot to allocate the per-CPU SDEI normal and critical stacks. It loops over every possible CPU; for each CPU it calls _init_sdei_stack for the normal stack pointer and then for the critical one, each of which calls arch_alloc_vmap_stack(SDEI_STACK_SIZE, cpu_to_node(cpu)) and stores the result in the per-CPU pointer, or returns -ENOMEM if the allocation returned NULL. The loop stops at the first failure. Return paths: there is one return, at the end. If no allocation failed it returns 0 with a normal and a critical stack stored for each possible CPU. If an allocation failed it first calls free_sdei_stacks(), which walks all possible CPUs and for each non-NULL normal or critical stack pointer sets it to NULL and vfree()s the stack (so stacks stored before the failure are released, as is any stack that was already present), and then returns -ENOMEM.
note: Contract cleared: function reads and writes per-CPU globals and allocates, which a result-only contract cannot state (reviewer round 15 right on that). Prose now says -ENOMEM and that free_sdei_stacks frees any non-NULL pointer on every possible CPU (sdei.c:49-65, 86-106). The iff-success claim is correct: err is only 0 if no _init_sdei_stack failed.

name: init_sdei_scs
prose: Static function with no arguments, run at boot to allocate the per-CPU SDEI shadow call stacks. Return paths: (1) if scs_is_enabled() is false it returns 0 immediately without allocating; (2) otherwise it loops over every possible CPU, calling _init_sdei_scs for the normal and then the critical shadow-call-stack pointer, each of which calls scs_alloc(cpu_to_node(cpu)) and stores the result in the per-CPU pointer or returns -ENOMEM if scs_alloc returned NULL; the loop stops at the first failure. If no allocation failed it returns 0. If an allocation failed it calls free_sdei_scs(), which walks all possible CPUs and for each non-NULL pointer sets it to NULL and calls scs_free(), and then returns -ENOMEM.
note: Contract cleared: global per-CPU state and allocation are involved (sdei.c:141-162, _init_sdei_scs and free_sdei_scs read above it). Reviewer round 15 right that the contract omitted them; the iff-success wording in the old prose is accurate.

name: restore_sve_fpsimd_context
prose: Static function (this is the CONFIG_ARM64_SVE definition; without that option a stub of the same name calls WARN_ON_ONCE(1) and returns -EINVAL) that restores SVE or streaming-SVE state from the signal frame context user->sve. Return paths in order: (1) -EINVAL if user->sve_size < sizeof(*user->sve), nothing modified; (2) the error from __get_user_error (-EFAULT) if reading the vl or flags fields fails, nothing modified; (3) with sm = flags & SVE_SIG_FLAG_SM and fpsimd_only = (user->sve_size == sizeof(*user->sve)): if sm is set, -EINVAL when SME is unsupported or fpsimd_only is true, else vl = task_get_sme_vl(current); if sm is clear, -EINVAL when SVE is unsupported and fpsimd_only is false, else vl = task_get_sve_vl(current); (4) -EINVAL if the context vl differs from vl; (5) if fpsimd_only, the result of restore_fpsimd_context(user): -EINVAL if user->fpsimd_size != sizeof(struct fpsimd_context), -EFAULT if the user copy fails, otherwise 0 after clearing TIF_SVE, clearing SVCR.SM, setting fp_type to FP_STATE_FPSIMD and calling fpsimd_update_current_state (TIF_SME is not touched); (6) -EINVAL if user->sve_size < SVE_SIG_CONTEXT_SIZE(vq); (7) if sm, -ENOMEM when sme_alloc(current, false) leaves thread.sme_state NULL (no flag change); (8) -ENOMEM when sve_alloc(current, true) leaves thread.sve_state NULL, after clearing TIF_SVE (a sme_state obtained at step 7 is left in place); (9) after this point thread state is changed: if sm, SVCR.SM is set and TIF_SME set (TIF_SVE not cleared); otherwise SVCR.SM is cleared and TIF_SVE set (TIF_SME not cleared); fp_type is set to FP_STATE_SVE in both cases; then -EFAULT if the copy of SVE_SIG_REGS_SIZE(vq) bytes into thread.sve_state fails (the payload may be partially copied); then the error of read_fpsimd_context (-EINVAL if user->fpsimd_size != sizeof(struct fpsimd_context), -EFAULT on copy failure), with the earlier changes kept; (10) otherwise fpsimd_update_current_state is called to merge the FPSIMD registers into the SVE state and it returns 0. sme_alloc and sve_alloc may reuse an existing buffer; no locks are taken and no references acquired.
note: Reviewer round 15 (fp_type should be FP_STATE_SME when SM set) is wrong: signal.c:517 sets FP_STATE_SVE unconditionally after the sm branch. Round 2 (newly allocated/zeroed) is wrong about the prose, which already says buffers may be reused. Original (other TIF flag not cleared) is right and already stated: 247-253. Slice cut the tail; read real file arch/arm64/kernel/signal.c:430-527, restore_fpsimd_context 316-333, read_fpsimd_context 298-314.

name: __kvm_find_s1_desc_level
prose: Function __kvm_find_s1_desc_level(vcpu, va, ipa, level) with level an int pointer; it walks the guest stage-1 page tables for va looking for the table whose IPA matches ipa. It sets the translation regime to TR_EL20 or TR_EL2 (depending on vcpu_el2_e2h_is_set) if is_hyp_ctxt(vcpu), else TR_EL10, and calls setup_s1_walk. Return paths: (1) it returns the nonzero result of setup_s1_walk without touching *level; (2) if the walk result level is S1_MMU_DISABLED it warns once, sets *level = 0 and returns 0; (3) otherwise it runs walk_s1 inside scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu), which takes the SRCU read lock on vcpu->kvm->srcu and releases it when the guarded statement ends; then if walk_s1 returned -EINTR (the match_s1_desc filter found a table with the wanted IPA) it sets *level = the matched level and returns 0; if walk_s1 returned 0 (walk completed with no match) it returns -ENOENT with *level unchanged; any other walk_s1 result is returned unchanged with *level unchanged.
note: Slice cut the head: the real name is __kvm_find_s1_desc_level (at.c:1562, level is int *, not u8 * as the old prose said). Old claim that the caller must not hold the SRCU lock removed: nothing in the code checks it. Match callback match_s1_desc at at.c:1546-1560 returns 0 on mismatch and -EINTR with the level on match.

name: check_all_fgt_masks
prose: Static __init function taking an int ret (an error code accumulated by earlier initialisation). It calls check_fgt_masks on each of the eleven FGT mask sets in its table (hfgrtr, hfgwtr, hfgitr, hdfgrtr, hdfgwtr, hafgrtr, hfgrtr2, hfgwtr2, hfgitr2, hdfgrtr2, hdfgwtr2), with no early exit regardless of ret or of earlier results. Each check_fgt_masks call logs an error per bit set in both the mask and nmask of that set (and then yields -EINVAL), recomputes that set res0 as ~(mask | nmask), and logs an info line if the new res0 differs from the old. The single return is ret ?: err: it returns ret if ret is non-zero, otherwise err, the bitwise OR of the eleven results, which is 0 or -EINVAL.
note: Contract cleared: the function mutates global mask structures and logs, so a result-only contract is incomplete (reviewers rounds 1-15 flagged that EINVAL was missing from the contract). Return expression at emulate-nested.c:2224 (slice 245); check_fgt_masks at 2180-2203 returns only 0 or -EINVAL.

name: kvm_vm_ioctl_mte_copy_tags
prose: Function taking kvm and copy_tags (guest_ipa, length, addr, flags, reserved). write is true when KVM_ARM_TAGS_FROM_GUEST is not set in flags, i.e. tags are written into the guest. Return paths before the lock: -EINVAL if kvm_has_mte(kvm) is false, if reserved[0] or reserved[1] is non-zero, if flags has bits other than KVM_ARM_TAGS_FROM_GUEST, if length or guest_ipa is not page-aligned, or if length > INT_MAX. It then takes kvm->slots_lock; every later exit goes through the out label, which releases that lock. With the lock held: if write and kvm->nr_memslots_dirty_logging is non-zero it sets ret = -EBUSY. Otherwise it loops one page at a time while length > 0: if __gfn_to_page returns NULL, or the page is not an online page (ZONE_DEVICE; the page is released unused), ret = -EFAULT and it leaves the loop; for a read it copies the page tags to the user buffer (or zeroes the user buffer if the page has no tags) and releases the page clean; for a write it copies tags from the user buffer into the page, clears the page tags if that copy was short, marks the page tagged and releases it dirty; if the number of tags copied is not MTE_GRANULES_PER_PAGE it sets ret = -EFAULT and leaves the loop; otherwise it advances gfn and the tag pointer and reduces length by PAGE_SIZE. At out, after unlocking: if length differs from the original copy_tags->length it returns copy_tags->length - length (the bytes of completed pages, positive; this is also what is returned, rather than 0, when every page was processed and copy_tags->length is non-zero); otherwise it returns ret, which is 0 only when copy_tags->length was 0, and is -EBUSY or -EFAULT if the failure happened before any page completed.
note: Reviewer round 15 is right: on full completion length reaches 0, so the check at guest.c:1080 returns copy_tags->length, not 0; old prose was wrong. Slice cut the head; read guest.c:975-1081. No lock is held on the -EINVAL early returns (lines 985-998).

name: __sysreg_restore_el1_state
prose: Static inline function taking ctxt, midr and mpidr; it returns nothing and takes no locks. It writes midr to VPIDR_EL2 and mpidr to VMPIDR_EL2. Then, depending on the first condition that holds: (a) if has_vhe() or the ARM64_WORKAROUND_SPECULATIVE_AT capability is not set, it writes SCTLR_EL1 and TCR_EL1 from ctxt; (b) otherwise, if ctxt->__hyp_running_vcpu is NULL, it writes TCR_EL1 from ctxt with TCR_EPD1_MASK and TCR_EPD0_MASK also set and then executes isb(); SCTLR_EL1 is not written, and this function does not later write TCR_EL1 in this case; (c) otherwise (non-VHE, workaround present, __hyp_running_vcpu non-NULL) neither is written yet. It then writes CPACR_EL1, TTBR0_EL1 and TTBR1_EL1 from ctxt; if ctxt_has_tcrx(ctxt) it writes TCR2_EL1, and within that also PIR_EL1 and PIRE0_EL1 if ctxt_has_s1pie(ctxt) and POR_EL1 if ctxt_has_s1poe(ctxt); it then writes ESR_EL1, AFSR0_EL1, AFSR1_EL1, FAR_EL1, MAIR_EL1, VBAR_EL1, CONTEXTIDR_EL1, AMAIR_EL1, CNTKCTL_EL1, PAR_EL1 and TPIDR_EL1 from ctxt; it writes TFSR_EL1 and TFSRE0_EL1 if ctxt_has_mte(ctxt), and, in case (c) only, executes isb(), writes SCTLR_EL1, executes isb() and writes TCR_EL1 from ctxt. Finally it writes SP_EL1, ELR_EL1 and SPSR_EL1 from ctxt and SCTLR2_EL1 if ctxt_has_sctlr2(ctxt).
note: Reviewer round 15 right: in case (b) the TCR write comes before the isb (sysreg-sr.h:227-230); old prose said after. Original rejection (SCTLR/TCR not always restored) was already reflected in the old prose. Slice cut the tail; the rest (MTE, final isb block, SP/ELR/SPSR/SCTLR2) was read from the real sysreg-sr.h after line 258.

name: host_stage2_adjust_range
prose: Static function taking addr and a struct kvm_mem_range pointer range; the caller must hold host_mmu.lock (hyp_assert_lock_held). It looks up the leaf entry for addr in the host stage-2 table with kvm_pgtable_get_leaf, giving pte and level. Return paths: (1) the error returned by kvm_pgtable_get_leaf, if non-zero; (2) -EAGAIN if kvm_pte_valid(pte); (3) -EPERM if pte is non-zero but not valid (with a WARN_ON if addr_is_memory(addr) and its host page state is not PKVM_NOPAGE); (4) with pte zero, it walks levels from the leaf level up to KVM_PGTABLE_LAST_LEVEL (towards smaller granules), skipping levels that do not support block mapping; for each candidate it forms the granule-aligned range containing addr, and if that range is not included in the input *range and the level is not the last level it tries the next level, otherwise it stores that range in *range and returns 0 (so the first, largest, candidate contained in the input range is chosen, and at the last level the candidate is taken even if it extends beyond the input range); (5) if the loop ends without choosing a level (only possible when no level from the leaf level through the last level supports block mapping, including the last level) it issues WARN_ON(1) and returns -EINVAL. *range is written only in the success case at (4).
note: Slice cut the head; read mem_protect.c:491-535. Old claim that *range is unchanged on every error path holds (only write is the success assignment at slice line 18). Original reviewer point (smallest vs largest, last level may exceed range) is right for the last-level case and is now stated; wording about direction of levels corrected.

name: host_stage2_idmap_locked
prose: Function taking addr, size and prot; the caller must hold host_mmu.lock. It returns the value of host_stage2_try(__host_stage2_idmap, addr, addr + size, prot): the macro asserts the lock is held, calls __host_stage2_idmap (kvm_pgtable_stage2_map of the identity mapping for [addr, addr + size) with prot, using host_s2_pool), and if that returns -ENOMEM it calls host_stage2_unmap_dev_all and, if that returns 0, calls __host_stage2_idmap once more. The result is 0 on success or the negative error code of the last step tried. It takes and releases no lock.
note: Callee host_stage2_try macro read at mem_protect.c:468-482; the retry on -ENOMEM was missing from the old prose, otherwise the old iff-zero statement is correct.

name: host_stage2_set_owner_locked
prose: Function taking addr, size and owner_id; the caller must hold host_mmu.lock. Return paths: (1) -EPERM if range_is_memory(addr, addr + size) is false, with no change made; (2) the non-zero result of host_stage2_try(kvm_pgtable_stage2_set_owner, &host_mmu.pgt, addr, size, &host_s2_pool, owner_id), returned without changing the vmemmap host page state (host_stage2_try retries once after host_stage2_unmap_dev_all if the first attempt returned -ENOMEM); (3) otherwise it sets the host page state of every page in [addr, addr + size) to PKVM_PAGE_OWNED if owner_id == PKVM_ID_HOST and to PKVM_NOPAGE for any other owner_id, and returns 0. It takes and releases no lock.
note: Old prose accurate; added the -ENOMEM retry in host_stage2_try. mem_protect.c slice lines 39-58.

name: host_stage2_force_pte_cb
prose: Static function taking addr, end and prot, with no side effects; it reads the memory-region table through range_is_memory(addr, end). If range_is_memory(addr, end) is true it returns (prot != PKVM_HOST_MEM_PROT); otherwise it returns (prot != PKVM_HOST_MMIO_PROT). Thus it requests page-level mappings for any protection other than the default one for that kind of range.
note: Slice lines 60-80; single if/else with a return in each branch.

name: host_stage2_idmap
prose: Static function taking a fault address addr. Before taking any lock it calls find_mem_range(addr, &range): the return value being non-NULL selects prot = PKVM_HOST_MEM_PROT, otherwise PKVM_HOST_MMIO_PROT (range is filled in either way). It then calls host_lock_component(); if host_stage2_adjust_range(addr, &range) returns non-zero that value is the result (no mapping is made); otherwise the result is host_stage2_idmap_locked(range.start, range.end - range.start, prot), 0 or a negative error code. host_unlock_component() is called before the single return on both paths.
note: Old claim that the lock is taken on every path was imprecise (find_mem_range runs before the lock); both returns go through the unlock label (slice 91-100).

name: handle_host_mem_abort
prose: Function taking the host cpu context host_ctxt (not used in the body); it returns nothing. It reads ESR_EL2 and calls __get_fault_info(esr, &fault). Return paths: (1) if __get_fault_info returns false it returns immediately (treated as a raced page-table change) without mapping anything; (2) otherwise it hits BUG_ON if the HPFAR_EL2 NS bit is not set in fault.hpfar_el2, computes addr = FIELD_GET(HPFAR_EL2_FIPA, fault.hpfar_el2) << 12, calls host_stage2_idmap(addr), hits BUG_ON if that returns a non-zero value other than -EAGAIN, and returns normally when the result is 0 or -EAGAIN.
note: Slice 103-128; old prose consistent with the code, wording tightened.

name: __host_check_page_state_range
prose: Static function taking addr, size and an expected host page state. It first calls check_range_allowed_memory(addr, addr + size) and returns its non-zero result (-EINVAL if the range crosses a memory/MMIO range boundary, -EPERM if it is not memory or is MEMBLOCK_NOMAP). It then asserts host_mmu.lock is held (hyp_assert_lock_held) and checks the host state of each page in the range: it returns -EPERM at the first page whose host state differs from state, and returns 0 if all match. It modifies no state.
note: Slice 155-172; check_range_allowed_memory read at mem_protect.c:430-447.

name: __host_set_page_state_range
prose: Static function taking addr, size and a page state; the caller holds host_mmu.lock. If the host state of the first page (at addr only) is PKVM_NOPAGE it calls host_stage2_idmap_locked(addr, size, PKVM_HOST_MEM_PROT) and, if that returns non-zero, returns that error without changing any page state. Otherwise, or after the idmap succeeded, it sets the host state of every page in [addr, addr + size) to state and returns 0.
note: Slice 174-187; old prose correct.

name: __hyp_check_page_state_range
prose: Static function taking phys, size and an expected hyp page state. It examines the hyp state of each page in [phys, phys + size) in order, returns -EPERM at the first page whose state differs from state, and returns 0 if all pages match. It does not modify state and takes no lock.

name: guest_get_page_state
prose: Static function taking a stage-2 pte and addr (addr is not used). If kvm_pte_valid(pte) is false it returns PKVM_NOPAGE; otherwise it returns pkvm_getstate(kvm_pgtable_stage2_pte_prot(pte)). It has no side effects.

name: __pkvm_host_share_hyp
prose: Function taking a page frame number pfn; phys = hyp_pfn_to_phys(pfn), size = PAGE_SIZE. It takes the host component lock and then the hyp component lock, and both are released (hyp first, then host) before its single return. Return paths: (1) the non-zero result of __host_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_OWNED), with nothing changed; (2) the non-zero result of __hyp_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_NOPAGE) (which is -EPERM), with nothing changed; (3) otherwise it sets the hyp state of the page to PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_BORROWED and calls __host_set_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_OWNED), wrapped in WARN_ON so a failure there only warns; it returns 0 in this case.
note: Slice 225-249. The old precondition that pfn maps allowed memory is not a precondition: a bad range makes the first check fail (-EINVAL or -EPERM from check_range_allowed_memory), so the return is not just 0 or -EPERM.

name: __pkvm_host_unshare_hyp
prose: Function taking a page frame number pfn; phys = hyp_pfn_to_phys(pfn), virt = __hyp_va(phys), size = PAGE_SIZE. It takes the host component lock and then the hyp component lock, and releases both (hyp first, then host) before its single return. Return paths, with no state changed on any of them: the non-zero result of __host_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_OWNED); the non-zero result of __hyp_check_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_SHARED_BORROWED) (-EPERM); -EBUSY if hyp_page_count((void *)virt) is non-zero. Otherwise it sets the hyp state of the page to PKVM_NOPAGE and calls __host_set_page_state_range(phys, size, PKVM_PAGE_OWNED), wrapped in WARN_ON so a failure only warns, and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the tail; read real mem_protect.c:754-781. Old text presented the shared state as a precondition although the function checks it and returns an error.

name: hyp_create_idmap
prose: Function taking hyp_va_bits (the hypervisor VA width), with no failure path of its own. It sets start to the physical address of __hyp_idmap_text_start rounded down to PAGE_SIZE and end to that of __hyp_idmap_text_end rounded up to PAGE_SIZE. It then sets the global __io_map_base to BIT(hyp_va_bits - 2) if bit (hyp_va_bits - 2) of start is clear, and to 0 if that bit of start is set (start is masked with that bit and the result is inverted with XOR, so no other bit of start is kept), and sets the global __hyp_vmemmap to __io_map_base | BIT(hyp_va_bits - 3). It returns the result of __pkvm_create_mappings(start, end - start, start, PAGE_HYP_EXEC), which maps the idmap text at its physical address with executable hyp permissions under pkvm_pgd_lock and returns the error code of kvm_pgtable_hyp_map (0 on success, otherwise a negative error). The shifts are only well-defined if hyp_va_bits >= 3 and hyp_va_bits - 2 is less than the width of unsigned long.
note: Reviewer round 15 is right: the code masks start with BIT(hyp_va_bits - 2) before the XOR (mm.c slice lines 172-173), so __io_map_base is not start with a bit toggled; old prose wrong. Reviewer round 2 (IO and vmemmap placed in disjoint quarters) is moot: the prose does not say that, and the code uses the lower/upper half of one quarter per the comment at 164-171. __pkvm_create_mappings read at mm.c:35-44.

name: kvm_pgd_pages
prose: Static function taking ia_bits and start_level that returns the number of pages in the stage-2 or hyp PGD: it builds a local struct kvm_pgtable with those two fields and returns kvm_pgd_page_idx(&pgt, -1ULL) + 1, converted to u32. kvm_pgd_page_idx computes (addr & (BIT(ia_bits) - 1)) >> kvm_granule_shift(start_level - 1), so the result is (((BIT(ia_bits)) - 1) >> kvm_granule_shift(start_level - 1)) + 1 truncated to 32 bits. It has no side effects. The expression is only well-defined when ia_bits is less than 64 and kvm_granule_shift(start_level - 1) is less than 64 (the source comment says the shift may underflow; for 4K pages that excludes start_level values that give a level below -2).
note: Contract cleared: it depended on BIT and the granule-shift definition. Reviewer round 15 is right that start_level = -3 gives an out-of-range shift (granule shift of level -4 is 9*(4-(-4))+3 = 75 for 4K pages), so the old precondition [-3, 4] was wrong; the PAGE_SHIFT remark is also right since kvm_granule_shift includes it. Source pgtable.c:56-72 and kvm_granule_shift in asm/kvm_pgtable.h:154.

name: __vgic_v3_get_gic_config
prose: Function taking no arguments that returns a u64 describing the GIC CPU interface. Return paths: (1) if cpus_have_final_cap(ARM64_HAS_GICV5_CPUIF) is true it returns read_gicreg(ICH_VTR_EL2) unchanged (no masking and no bit 63 handling); (2) otherwise it reads ICC_SRE_EL1 into sre; on VHE it saves the interrupt mask state with local_daif_save, on nVHE it sets HCR_AMO, HCR_FMO and HCR_IMO with sysreg_clear_set_hcr and executes isb; it writes 0 to ICC_SRE_EL1, isb, reads ICC_SRE_EL1 back into val, writes sre back to ICC_SRE_EL1, isb; on VHE it restores the saved mask state with local_daif_restore, on nVHE it clears HCR_AMO, HCR_FMO and HCR_IMO (regardless of whether they were set before the function ran) and executes isb; it then returns (val has ICC_SRE_EL1_SRE set ? 0 : (1ULL << 63)) OR read_gicreg(ICH_VTR_EL2), so bit 63 is set exactly when SRE read back as clear, and the other bits are those read from ICH_VTR_EL2 (documented as bits 31:0, with RES0 above). ICC_SRE_EL1 is restored to its entry value on the non-GICv5 path.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the GICv5 return at vgic-v3-sr.c slice line 183 is the raw ICH_VTR_EL2 read, so old claim that bit 63 is clear was unsupported. Reviewer round 2 (nVHE uses set via sysreg_clear_set_hcr) is already what the old prose said (set then clear); not an error in the prose. New wording also removes the claim that interrupt-mask state is left as on entry for nVHE: HCR bits are cleared, not restored (slice 221).
